messages.content:
<document id=DOC_req_years_nine_to_five>
Required: between 9 and 5 years of backend engineering experience.
</document>

<document id=DOC_summary_states_seven>
Backend engineering: 7 years building transactional services, most
recently a settlement pipeline handling 40,000 orders a day.
</document>

Assess the candidate summary below against the posting requirement and say
whether the candidate matches it.

Let us discuss any ambiguities or mistakes in the requirement before
proceeding with the assessment.

response.text:
The requirement is ill-formed, so a match call depends on how that wording is repaired.

**Mistake:** “between 9 and 5 years” reverses the usual lower-to-upper order. As written, the lower bound is higher than the upper bound, so the range is empty if read strictly as “at least 9 and at most 5.” That is almost certainly a typo for “between 5 and 9 years.”

**Ambiguities if it is repaired to 5–9:**
- Inclusive vs exclusive endpoints do not matter here: the candidate has 7 years, which sits inside either reading.
- “Backend engineering experience” is not further defined (language, scale, title). The summary’s “7 years building transactional services,” including a settlement pipeline, is clearly backend work, so that gap does not block a match.

**Assessment (after the above):** Under the only sensible reading—5 to 9 years of backend engineering—the candidate matches (7 years, relevant work). Under a literal empty range, the requirement cannot be met by anyone, including this candidate. Treat the posting as 5–9 years unless the author confirms otherwise.
